## Proof

Let $\mathfrak c = |\mathbb R| = 2^{\aleph_0}$. Define the sequence of cardinals
$$\kappa_0 = \mathfrak c, \qquad \kappa_{n+1} = 2^{\kappa_n}.$$

**Claim 1.** $|V_n| = \kappa_n$ for every $n < \omega$.

*Proof by induction.* The base case is $|V_0| = |\mathbb R| = \mathfrak c = \kappa_0$. For the inductive step, by Cantor's theorem $|\mathcal P(V_n)| = 2^{|V_n|} > |V_n|$, so
$$|V_{n+1}| = |V_n \cup \mathcal P(V_n)| = \max(|V_n|,\, 2^{|V_n|}) = 2^{|V_n|} = 2^{\kappa_n} = \kappa_{n+1}. \quad\square$$

**Claim 2.** $|\mathbb V| = \sup_{n<\omega} \kappa_n =: \kappa_\omega$.

Since $\mathbb V = \bigcup_{n<\omega} V_n$ is an increasing union and $|V_n| = \kappa_n$ is strictly increasing (Cantor), the cardinality of the union is the supremum:
$$|\mathbb V| = \sup_{n<\omega} \kappa_n = \kappa_\omega.$$

In standard beth-notation this is $\beth_\omega$ (with $\beth_0 = \aleph_0$, $\beth_1 = \mathfrak c$, so $\kappa_n = \beth_{n+1}$ and $\kappa_\omega = \beth_\omega$). Note $\kappa_\omega$ is a **strong limit cardinal** of **cofinality $\omega$**: for every $\lambda < \kappa_\omega$ we have $2^\lambda < \kappa_\omega$, and $\operatorname{cf}(\kappa_\omega) = \omega$ since the sequence $\langle \kappa_n : n < \omega\rangle$ is cofinal and strictly increasing of length $\omega$.

**Claim 3.** $|\mathcal P_{fin}(\mathbb V)| = \kappa_\omega$.

For any infinite set $X$ with $|X| = \kappa$, the family of finite subsets satisfies
$$\mathcal P_{fin}(X) = \bigcup_{n < \omega} [X]^{n}, \qquad |[X]^n| \le |X^n| = \kappa^n = \kappa \;\;(\text{for } n \ge 1),$$
and $|[X]^1| = \kappa$, so $|\mathcal P_{fin}(X)| = \kappa \cdot \aleph_0 = \kappa$.

Applying this to $X = \mathbb V$ (which is infinite, indeed $|\mathbb V| = \kappa_\omega \ge \mathfrak c$):
$$|\mathcal P_{fin}(\mathbb V)| = |\mathbb V| = \kappa_\omega.$$

**Conclusion.** Both sets have the same cardinality:
$$\boxed{|\mathbb V| = |\mathcal P_{fin}(\mathbb V)| = \beth_\omega = \sup_{n<\omega} \beth_n\;\;(\text{with } \beth_1 = \mathfrak c).}$$

Equivalently, writing $\kappa_0 = |\mathbb R|$ and $\kappa_{n+1} = 2^{\kappa_n}$, both cardinalities equal $\sup_{n<\omega}\kappa_n$. The key points are: (i) each stage $V_{n+1}$ has cardinality $2^{|V_n|}$ by Cantor, giving the iterated power-set growth; (ii) the union over $\omega$ many stages yields the supremum $\kappa_\omega = \beth_\omega$, a strong-limit cardinal of cofinality $\omega$; (iii) the finite-subset construction does not increase cardinality for infinite sets, so $\mathcal P_{fin}(\mathbb V)$ has the same size as $\mathbb V$.
